To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pre-school children show an overall left-haemisphere bias for visual letter perception, (2) this bias is enhanced by a sensori-motory (printing) learning phase, (3) enhanced visual letter recognition in the sensori-motry group is associated with increased activation in the occipital cortex and (4) the results provide evidence for the role of learning-by-doing in the development of the neural systems for visual letter recognition in pre-school children.
